message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large.  It is commonly quoted as the **Shannon number**, which is roughly

\[
N \approx 10^{43}\text{–}10^{46}
\]

(about 1 × 10^43 to 1 × 10^46).  This estimate comes from counting all possible ways the pieces can be arranged on the board while respecting the rules of chess (e.g., pawn placement, king safety, castling rights, en‑passant possibilities, etc.).  In short, there are on the order of a few hundred trillion trillion trillion possible arrangements.
